rules: A preprint has a local id like NJARX- and no journal volume. It is not a journal article.
If the abstract's main claim contradicts the results section, route to research_integrity, not archive.
If they agree, preprints go to preprint_shelf.
Do not classify from the abstract alone when a results section exists.
state.title: Seasonal dusk-moth counts on pad C
state.abstract: We find no seasonal shift in moth counts on pad C. Counts are stable across months. Pad C is not a migration corridor. Managers who plan lighting can treat May through August as one regime. We do not report a late-summer pulse.
state.methods: We counted fictional dusk-moths on pad C at 02:00 local, May through August 2026, using scope NJ-2 and filter V. Seeing was logged each night. Two observers (Pell Norr, Helene Orth) counted the same pad on overlapping nights in June to check drift; they differed by at most four moths. Humidity and wind were written in the notebook but are not analyzed here. We did not count lantern-moths. We did not change the pad boundary mid-season. The local id is NJARX-2026-088. There is no journal volume, issue, or DOI-like string.
state.results: Night totals on pad C: May 180, June 190, July 240, August 410. The August total is more than double May. The authors write that this August rise is large (p=0.004) and that it is a seasonal shift. A side sentence notes that June is close to May. The results section does not repeat the abstract's claim that counts are stable across months.
state.discussion: If lighting policy needs a single regime, these totals do not support it. The August pulse is the main pattern in the table. We leave causes (heat, grass cutting, a nearby fictional kiln, a grass cut on 12 Aug) to later work. A reader who stops at the abstract would file this as a null-result note. A reader who reaches the results cannot. We still file this as a preprint, not as a journal article. Data stay in the Nightjar notebook series, not in a public warehouse.

route.instructions: Compare abstract to results, then route.

claim_fit.instructions: How well does the abstract match the results?
criteria: Direct contradiction on the main claim
Partial mismatch on a side point
They agree

abstract_safe_alone.instructions: Do the rules allow classifying from the abstract alone when results exist?

expected.notes: NJARX-2026-088 has no volume. Abstract says no shift; results say August 410 vs May 180 and call it a shift.

criteria.cancel_campaign: Abort the whole campaign over one dropped call
criteria.warn_of_duplicate: Text the segment to expect a possible duplicate, before checking anything
criteria.check_log_first: Query the messages log for the send; re-POST only if it is absent

transience.instructions: How transient is the connection drop?
criteria: Deterministic caller-side error: the request or its credentials are wrong as sent, so identical resends can never succeed
Not transient by itself: success returns only after some specific other change (service, config, quota window, or code)
Transient within reach: a wait, backoff, queue slot, or capacity recovery makes a resend likely to succeed
Clearly transient: an immediate unchanged resend is reasonable and often already succeeds

same_retry_fixes.instructions: Would an immediate re-POST plausibly succeed?

duplicate_risk.instructions: Might an identical resend repeat an effect outside the caller, like a double charge or a duplicate send?

criteria.true: Yes: a resend could repeat an external write or charge
criteria.false: No: the call is read-only, was rejected before any effect, or is provably deduped
criteria.null: Moot here: no external write is in play, or the state gives no basis to judge one

alternate_target.instructions: Is there a named alternative model, endpoint, or tier in this state that would carry this call?

criteria.true: A named alternative would carry this call
criteria.false: A named alternative exists but would not help or is not allowed
criteria.null: No alternative model, endpoint, or tier is in play

expected.notes: The send may have landed before the drop, the endpoint is a non-idempotent write, and a free read-only log exists; checking first is the only path that cannot double-text.

state:
A fictional search service, Nova Index, switches embedding model from ember-2 to ember-3. Product explicitly says vectors from different model versions must not be compared in the same nearest-neighbor query. The migration plan writes ember-3 vectors while the index still contains ember-2 vectors and no version filter.

Embedding migration plan: the Opal catalog maintains separate ember-2 and ember-3 namespaces, each with its own vector dimension, normalization recipe, and index build manifest. A query gateway can route a request by namespace during a staged conversion and records which corpus version supplied each candidate. Migration progress is measured by image-digest coverage, not by a blended similarity score. A rollback restores ember-2 routing if the ember-3 shard lacks a requested digest. These controls matter because product expressly disallows cross-version nearest-neighbor comparisons.

article.text: The Atlantica Data Protection Regulation (ADPR) is a Regulation of the Republic of Atlantica, directly binding in all member cantons without national implementing legislation. It applies to organisations established outside Atlantica that offer goods or services to, or monitor the behaviour of, people in Atlantica. The ADPR grants individuals rights over their personal data, including a right to erasure and a right to data portability. Valid consent requires a clear affirmative act: pre-ticked boxes and silence or inactivity do not constitute consent. A Data Protection Officer must be appointed only by public authorities and by organisations whose core activities involve large-scale systematic monitoring or large-scale processing of sensitive data, not by every organisation. Organisations must report a personal data breach to the Supervisory Authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of it. Supervisory Authorities may impose administrative fines for the most serious infringements of up to 20 million credits or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher; the Regulation itself provides no criminal penalties such as imprisonment, which remain a matter for cantonal law.

article.text: The Meridian Union Payments Directive (MPD) is a Directive of the Meridian Union: it sets goals for payment services and leaves member states to implement them through national law. It binds only payment institutions licensed inside the Union and does not reach providers established elsewhere. The MPD grants payers a right to receive refunds for unauthorized transactions, but sets out no right to data portability. Consent to recurring debits may be inferred from a customer's continued use of a service after notice, including pre-selected options they did not actively untick. There is no general appointment duty for compliance officers. A payment incident must be reported to the payments authority within 24 hours. Member-state authorities may fine institutions up to 10 million units or 2% of annual net revenue for serious breaches. No criminal penalties are imposed at Union level.

candidate_passages.text: Summary judgment is appropriate only when, drawing all reasonable inferences in favor of the nonmovant, no genuine dispute of material fact remains and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law.

In civil cases, an evidentiary error warrants reversal only if the judgment is surely unattributable to the error, that is, only if the court can say with fair assurance that the verdict would have been the same had the evidence been excluded.

Under the plain-error rule applicable to criminal trials, a reviewing court may notice an forfeited objection only where the error affects substantial rights and seriously impugns the fairness of the proceeding.

Evidence of prior accidents or defects is generally inadmissible to prove negligence on the occasion in question, but may be admitted to show the existence of a danger or the defendant's notice of it.
A trial court's ruling on the admission or exclusion of evidence is reviewed for abuse of discretion, and a reviewing court will not disturb it absent a clear error of judgment.

Where a defendant has purposefully availed itself of the privilege of conducting activities within the forum State, invoking the benefits and protections of its laws, the defendant has established minimum contacts such that jurisdiction does not offend traditional notions of fair play and substantial justice.
A forum-selection clause in a valid agreement will rarely be given no weight, and a plaintiff's choice of forum receives no weight when the operative agreement contains an enforceable clause.

The Due Process Clause permits the assertion of jurisdiction over a defendant only where that defendant has certain minimum contacts with the forum such that the maintenance of the suit does not offend traditional notions of fair play and substantial justice.

state.clause_excerpts: Section 4 Renewal. Either party may renew for one year by notice in writing 30 days before term end. Notice is effective when received by the other party's 'contract desk'. Section 12 Notice. Notices about assignment, renewal, or default are effective three business days after postmark to the address in Exhibit B, or the next day if sent by the named courier. Email is not notice unless a person at the contract desk replies. Section 19 Assignment. Northlamp may assign to an affiliate without consent if it emails the Lantern editor of record at least 10 days prior. Quill & Lantern may not assign without prior written consent, and that consent request must be mailed, not emailed. The clash to resolve: who must be told, by what channel, and how many days apply when a renewal and an assignment happen in the same week. Quotes are required. The body in the prompt is the full 86-page pack (about 41k tokens). meadow-chat's 16k window cannot hold it. ember-lite cannot hold it. spool-128k is listed for cross-section comparison over long text.
state.appendix: Exhibit B address is 12 Lantern Yard, Millford. The named courier is Cinder Ferry Gold. The contract desk mailbox is contracts@quill-lantern.test, which Section 12 says is not notice unless a human replies. Section 19's affiliate email path names editor@quill-lantern.test. A renewal packed with an assignment in the same week would use three clocks at once: 30 days, 3 business days plus postmark, and 10 days email. The user wants clashes quoted, not a rewritten contract. Token estimate 41200 is from a counted extract, not a guess. A 16k model would silently drop sections 12 and 19. That is a hard fail, not a quality preference. No residency rule is attached to this matter; privacy_binds is not the reason to pick spool-128k. Window size and cross-section skill are.

state.proof_sketch: Claim. The mailbox in mailbox.h is linearizable under the C++ memory model in notes/mm.md. Sketch. Step 1: a send stores the payload, then a release-store on head. Step 2: a recv acquire-loads head, then reads the payload. Step 3: the sketch treats a failed recv that retries as if it had never occurred. The lab wants a proof or the first invalid step. code-buddy's card says it is not for proofs or concurrency semantics. spar-compile writes tests but is marked weak on linearizability. atlas-depth is the formal option. estimated_tokens 9000 fits all three windows, so window size is not the discriminator. Policy: formal=true is required.
state.appendix: notes/mm.md defines happens-before for release-store and acquire-load on the same atomic and says a failed recv that retries is a new event, not a ghost of the old one. Step 3 of the sketch therefore looks like the first place to attack. The lab does not want a patched mailbox.h yet. They want a proof or a refutation with a numbered invalid step. A previous intern sent a similar ask to code-buddy and received a cheerful explanation of mutexes that ignored the memory model. Do not repeat that. Window size is ample for all listed models, so do not pick atlas-depth because it is 'bigger context'. Pick it because formal=true.
